summary: Reproduced and fixed the Llama32 streaming parser corruption described in the issue. Its Python-dict compatibility regexes rewrote single-quote patterns inside already-valid double-quoted JSON string values, leaving invalid JSON and dropping the tool call. Streaming conversion now operates only outside double-quoted strings, while retaining support for single-quoted Python dict output.

tests.what_was_measured: 10 focused Llama32 detector tests passed, including failing-before regressions for both reported quote patterns, a cross-chunk boundary, and a boundary case retaining Python single-quoted dict conversion.
The complete shared function-call detector test module passed: 246 tests and 4 subtests.
All applicable repository formatting, lint, safety, and CI-registration hooks passed for the changed source and tests.

gpu_execution.evidence: The defect is deterministic post-detokenization string parsing and was reproduced directly against Llama32Detector on CPU. No model weights or GPU execution were needed or claimed.

remaining_limitations: No full model or HTTP serving reproduction was performed; this validates the actual detector implementation with fixed decoded model output only.
The issue reports independent defects in other detectors. This change intentionally fixes only the evidenced Llama32 JSON-string corruption.
The Python-dict fallback remains intentionally narrow and does not attempt to support every possible Python literal or escaped single-quoted string form.
